implementation_notes: Nokogiri is the dominant Ruby XML stack: XML::Builder's method-missing DSL (xml.li album.title) builds a document with escaping handled for you, and Nokogiri::XSLT.parse(xsl).transform(doc) runs libxslt for the declarative route; REXML ships with Ruby for small documents. ERB is the Template View alternative, so a transformer object is only justified when output is assembled programmatically across several formats.
code_sketch:
builder = Nokogiri::XML::Builder.new do |xml|
  xml.ul do
    artist.albums.each { |album| xml.li(album.title) }
  end
end
builder.to_xml
pitfalls: Builder uses method_missing: tag names that collide with Ruby methods (class, type, id) need a trailing underscore, as in xml.class_.
Nokogiri::XSLT does not safely process untrusted stylesheets: libxslt resolves external entities and can read the file system, so stylesheets are trusted code.
Without the |xml| block parameter the DSL runs in an instance_eval scope, making outer locals and self surprising inside the block.

variants.name: Nokogiri::XSLT stylesheet
variants.implementation_notes: The declarative route: Nokogiri::XSLT.parse compiles the stylesheet into a Stylesheet object whose transform(document, params) returns a result document, backed by libxslt. Choose it when presentation is a stylesheet and the model can be serialized to XML, and treat stylesheet input as trusted code.
variants.code_sketch:
xsl = Nokogiri::XSLT(File.read("artist.xsl"))
result = xsl.transform(Nokogiri::XML(artist_xml), ["locale", "'de'"])
puts result.to_xml
pitfalls: Parameters are passed as pre-quoted XPath-style strings (see quote_params); passing raw Ruby strings breaks expressions containing quotes.
The Nokogiri XSLT handler classes register globally: extension functions leak across requests unless the registration is intentional.
